idiom_name: one Sequelize model (or Knex table query) per concrete type
implementation_notes: In JavaScript a model already is a table - Sequelize's own wording is that 'a model is an abstraction that represents a table in your database' - so the pattern needs no inheritance mapping: declare one model class per concrete type, spread the shared columns in from a common attribute object or mixin, and use one Knex query builder per table when you prefer SQL. There is no framework union, so a mixed list is either several queries merged in code or an explicit UNION ALL with NULL padding and a literal type tag. Reconstructing the classic structure (a shared base model plus a union helper) is only worth it when the hierarchy is real and read polymorphically; otherwise plain per-table models stay simpler.
pitfalls: No key sharing: two models with a BIGINT primary key mean you own uniqueness across the hierarchy (one sequence, UUIDs or a shared key table).
Object spread duplicates the base attributes at model-definition time, so editing `base` silently changes every model without any migration for the existing tables.
There is no polymorphic fetch: a query per table (or a raw UNION ALL) is the only way to read the hierarchy, and every branch must pad the other subclasses' columns with NULL.
